name: Sherlock
summary: Check whether a public username appears across supported social platforms.
description: Sherlock is a locally run Python tool that checks public profile URL patterns and site responses for a supplied username. It is a lead-generation tool, not proof of identity.
when: Use when researching your own public username footprint or an account you have permission to assess.
where: Fedora/Linux terminal, macOS, Windows; consult official installation guide.
how: Install the supported package using pipx: pipx install sherlock-project
Open returned public URLs individually to confirm they genuinely match.
uses: Check username availability and potential name collisions
Research a public project's official account footprint
restrictions: Only public information is checked; private accounts and hidden data cannot be accessed.
False positives and stale site checks occur; matching usernames do not prove matching people.
Some sites impose rate limits, blocks, or terms on automated lookups; respect them.
Do not use it to track, harass, or expose private individuals.
pricingNote: Open-source local software; third-party sites may restrict automated checks.

name: ExifTool
summary: Read metadata from photos, documents, and other supported local files.
description: ExifTool is a metadata reader and writer supporting a wide range of file formats and metadata standards. Many photos and documents hold timestamps, camera data, or software identifiers.
when: Use when examining files that you own or have permission to inspect, particularly to check file metadata before sharing.
where: Local desktop command line, including Linux and macOS.
how: On Fedora, install from the package manager if available: sudo dnf install perl-Image-ExifTool
Inspect a file you own: exiftool myphoto.jpg
Review fields carefully; many apps strip metadata on upload.
uses: Detect accidental disclosure of location metadata before publishing
restrictions: Metadata may be absent, altered, or inaccurate; it is not a reliable proof of authenticity.
Support varies by file type and tag; reading does not imply writing support.
Avoid modifying source evidence; work on copies if you experiment with writing.
Only inspect files you are authorized to access.
pricingNote: Free local tool; no subscription required.

name: Wayback Machine
summary: Browse saved snapshots of public websites from earlier dates.
description: The Internet Archive's Wayback Machine lets visitors view captures of public websites, compare dated snapshots, and save some pages.
when: Use when checking how a website's public content, policy, or design changed over time.
where: Web browser on desktop or phone.
how: Visit the official Wayback Machine site.
Enter a public website URL and select an available snapshot date.
Cross-check the snapshot against other evidence and record the capture date.
uses: Verify past product descriptions and documentation
restrictions: Not every webpage is archived; snapshots may be incomplete or broken.
Interactive pages, JavaScript, and media are often imperfectly preserved.
Some content is excluded or removed by the archive.
A snapshot is historical evidence, not proof that a page was accurate when posted.
pricingNote: Free public browsing; archive coverage varies.

name: OpenStreetMap
description: OpenStreetMap is a collaboratively maintained map database useful for public streets, paths, landmarks, and geographic context.
when: Use to understand places, compare public map features, or build geographic context around a public story.
where: Web browser, mobile browser, and compatible map applications.
how: Search for a city, landmark, or public location.
Inspect features and attribution; compare with other sources if accuracy matters.
restrictions: Community coverage and accuracy vary by region.
Map data is licensed under ODbL; attribution and other obligations apply to reuse.
Public tile servers have usage policies and are not unlimited free hosting for third-party apps.
Do not treat a map label as verified ground truth.
pricingNote: Free data and website; specific third-party hosted services may cost money.

name: Wikimedia Commons
summary: Find freely licensed media with provenance and license notes.
description: Wikimedia Commons hosts images, audio, and other media, often with useful source, author, date, and license metadata.
when: Use when looking for publicly reusable reference media or checking the provenance of a published image.
how: Search Wikimedia Commons for a topic or place.
Open a file page to review author, date, source, and licensing.
Follow attribution and license conditions before reusing a file.
uses: Review a file's stated source and upload history
restrictions: Individual files have different licenses; some require attribution or share-alike.
Upload descriptions can contain mistakes and should be independently checked.
Availability does not override privacy, personality, or trademark rights.
Not all media is necessarily usable for every purpose.
pricingNote: Free access; reuse depends on the individual media license.

name: VirusTotal
summary: Check known security detections for files, hashes, and URLs.
description: VirusTotal aggregates signals from security products and community sources for submitted indicators. It helps triage suspicious content but cannot conclusively determine safety.
when: Use to research a suspicious URL or file hash while following your organization's privacy and data-sharing rules.
where: Browser and a restricted API tier; some services require paid access.
how: Search a known file hash or URL to see available existing reports.
Do not upload private or confidential files; review detections in context.
uses: Look up an existing file hash report
restrictions: The public/free API is limited and governed by usage terms; commercial use may require paid access.
Uploads may be shared with security partners; never submit private files casually.
False positives and false negatives are possible.
Paid functions and quotas are separate from free access.
pricingNote: Free public functionality with limits; premium API and products are paid.
